name: iOS background modes
plain: Xcode background modes (audio, location, VoIP, Bluetooth, fetch, push) decide what can run while closed.
meaning: Each mode is a narrow exemption tied to a visible use. Using one for something else is an App Review rejection, so the list shows what a company claims to need.

android.api_surface: Foreground service types as the closest analog
android.note: Android uses FGS types instead of per-mode entitlements

ios.permission: UIBackgroundModes: audio, location, voip, bluetooth-central, bluetooth-peripheral, fetch, remote-notification, processing, external-accessory, nearby-interaction
ios.revocation: Not user visible except Background App Refresh
ios.store_policy: App Review 2.5.4: modes only for stated purpose
ios.note: Modes have different run windows: audio until playback ends; location until stopped; fetch and processing as scheduled

limits.headline: Can run in the background on iPhone, but only for the kind of job Apple approved
limits.user_action: You start playback, a navigation trip, a call, or connect to a Bluetooth device
can: Keep playing audio after you leave the app, until playback ends
Keep tracking location until the app stops it, if you allowed Always
Wake up for an incoming call or a Bluetooth event
Refresh content now and then when the system decides it is a good time
cannot: Run any task it likes while closed; each mode covers one kind of job
Choose when fetch and processing happen, since iOS sets the schedule
Run in the background with no capability turned on in the app's setup
limits.reach_label: Ongoing, but only for approved jobs
limits.differs: Android has no per mode approval. It uses foreground service types and a visible notification instead.

story.what_it_is: iPhone only lets closed apps keep running for a few approved reasons, like music or navigation.

marketing.name: Background execution modes
marketing.pitch: Apple lets developers enable specific background capabilities such as audio, location, VoIP and Bluetooth in Xcode.

story.for_you: You see it as the colored bar or dot showing an app is using location or audio. It is why music keeps playing and a run keeps being recorded with the screen off.
story.for_makers: Makers must ask Apple for each mode and show a real need. The list tells reviewers what the app claims to do, and misuse can get an update rejected.

use_cases.example: A music app keeps playing with the phone locked using the audio mode.
A navigation app keeps giving turn by turn voice directions in your pocket.
A workout app records a bike ride route and heart rate while the screen is off.
A calling app wakes the phone for an incoming call using the VoIP mode.
A home app stays in touch with a Bluetooth lock so it can unlock as you arrive.
A multiplayer game uses the audio mode for in game voice chat that keeps going when you switch apps.

risks: Some apps stretch a mode to stay alive
Hard to tell which apps run in the background
story.android_note: Android uses foreground service types instead of one entitlement per mode.
story.ios_note: Each mode has its own run window, such as until music ends or until location is stopped.

abuse: Abusing audio or location for keep-alive

history.change: VoIP pushes must show a CallKit call
